ideas.title: Foldable tray
ideas.originalProblem: We need to find out which carrying or storage task a folding tray would help.
ideas.originalSolution: A folding oval tray with three compartments on one half.
ideas.improvedProblem: We need to find out which carrying or storage task a folding tray would help.
ideas.reason: A positive lock stops the centre joint folding while the tray is in use.

changes.why: Use a hinge and a positive open lock, then release the lock to fold the empty tray.

ideas.howItWorks: The hinge guides the two halves. A locking bridge below the joint supports both halves while open. Retract it before folding.
ideas.boundary: Guard the hinge gap; keep the bridge captive; define a rated load after testing. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check hinge clearance, lock engagement, load deflection and whether storage space improves.
ideas.question: Who needs a folding tray, and what must it hold?

ideas.title: Mobile bin and companion
ideas.originalProblem: A fixed disposal point may be inconvenient to reach.
ideas.originalSolution: A four-wheel bin with a peaked lid and a smaller wheeled companion.
ideas.improvedProblem: A fixed disposal point may be inconvenient to reach.
ideas.reason: The companion adds a second stream. Hands-free opening and deposit feedback give the mobile station a useful interaction.

changes.why: Link the pair for moving; add hands-free opening and deposit feedback. Use the companion for recycling.

ideas.boundary: Keep each box supported by its own wheels; lock it for use; guard the lid drive and hitch; stop closing if obstructed; provide manual opening and transport mode. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Compare the pair with two ordinary bins: turning space, parking, separation mistakes, hand contact, false lid openings and whether users notice the deposit feedback.
ideas.question: When would people choose this over two ordinary bins?
ideas.howItWorks: Push and park the pair. A proximity sensor opens the lid. A sensor inside detects a deposit and displays THANKS.
proposalParts: Four-wheel main body with peaked hinged lid
Proximity sensor, lid actuator, deposit sensor and display

ideas.title: Mushroom nightlight
ideas.originalProblem: An older person getting out of bed needs to see the nearby floor.
ideas.originalSolution: A mushroom lamp that turns on when the person sits up, with accessible charging.
ideas.improvedProblem: An older person getting out of bed needs to see the nearby floor.
ideas.reason: Good sensor placement and directed light matter more than the mushroom shape alone.

changes.why: Aim the light at the floor and keep the motion sensor clear of the shade.

ideas.howItWorks: The motion sensor signals a controller. The controller switches the LED on and times how long it stays lit. The ON/OFF control overrides it.
ideas.boundary: Provide cable strain relief, ventilation and a stable base; use a compatible power supply. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check detection from the actual bed, useful floor visibility, glare, timeout and OFF behavior.
ideas.question: What movement should turn it on, and which floor area should it light?

ideas.title: Robot sorting bin
ideas.originalProblem: People sometimes put items into the wrong compartment.
ideas.originalSolution: A robot guides rubbish into several labelled compartments.
ideas.improvedProblem: People sometimes put items into the wrong compartment.
ideas.reason: The sequence separates choosing, moving the guide and releasing the item, so the motion can be checked.

changes.why: Use a supported pivoting chute and select its position before loading one item.

ideas.boundary: Enclose moving parts; stop on obstruction; use an accessible service release and rated actuator supply. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Trace both routes, measure clearances and test jams with representative clean items.
ideas.question: Which part carries the item load, and which part only turns the diverter?
ideas.howItWorks: A person chooses a category. The servo tilts the chute left or right about a front-to-back shaft. Wait for the chute to settle, then put one item into the hopper.
ideas.reviewNotice: This proposal is under review. No replacement option has been chosen.

ideas.title: Sound and hello companion
ideas.originalProblem: A person living alone wants comfort and an easy way to send a greeting.
ideas.originalSolution: Switch the heart on, pat the plush to sing, and hold the paw to send Hello.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person living alone wants comfort and an easy way to send a greeting.
ideas.reason: Separate actions make it clearer what each control does and whether the greeting arrived.

changes.why: Keep a soft body around a removable control module, with separate sound and greeting controls.

ideas.howItWorks: A sound control starts or stops a chosen tune. The paw control sends a greeting to a paired receiver, which acknowledges it.
ideas.boundary: Secure the battery and paw wiring, bound the volume, remove electronics for washing and use a communication link that reaches the actual recipient. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Compare the original pat control with the clear button and measure missed or accidental activations.
ideas.question: How does the person know the greeting was received?

ideas.title: Private parcel box
ideas.originalProblem: A parcel left outside a door can be seen and reached by other people.
ideas.originalSolution: A parcel box with an angled transparent cover, string, pole and lock.
ideas.improvedProblem: A parcel left outside a door can be seen and reached by other people.
ideas.reason: Opaque panels conceal the contents. A controlled hinge and defined delivery cycle replace the uncertain cover linkage.

changes.why: Use a complete opaque rectangular enclosure with a conventional hinged lid and a real latch.

ideas.boundary: Use controlled lid closing, guarded hinge gaps, anchoring and drainage; privacy is not proof of theft resistance. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check parcel fit, closing force, latch engagement, owner access, water entry and second-delivery handling.
ideas.question: How can the next courier deliver after the first parcel has locked the box?
ideas.howItWorks: The courier puts a parcel into the prepared box. A rear hinge and folding two-link stay guide the lid. Closing it engages the latch; the owner unlocks the box to retrieve the parcel and reset it.

ideas.title: Water storing plant pot
ideas.originalProblem: Busy people can forget to water their plants.
ideas.originalSolution: A pot stores rain or wasted water and waters a plant when the soil is dry.
ideas.improvedProblem: Busy people can forget to water their plants.
ideas.reason: The wick provides a real water path; the cover keeps the stored water enclosed.

changes.why: Use a covered reservoir and a wick that reaches both the water and the soil.

ideas.howItWorks: Water moves through the wick into the inner pot. The refill cap gives access to the reservoir. A screened vent and overflow manage air and excess water.
ideas.boundary: Keep overflow below soil level; preserve drainage; use suitable water and cleanable parts. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Measure water delivery and soil condition with the actual plant, wick and reservoir height.
ideas.question: How much water reaches this plant over the interval it is usually left alone?

ideas.title: Doorbell wristband
ideas.originalProblem: A person with hearing difficulties may miss someone ringing the doorbell.
ideas.originalSolution: A wristband flashes and vibrates when the bell rings.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person with hearing difficulties may miss someone ringing the doorbell.
ideas.reason: Two adjustable cues help the wearer notice the event in different situations.

changes.why: Pair a doorbell transmitter with a wearable receiver and clear test or acknowledgement control.

ideas.boundary: Provide low-battery and link-status indication, secure battery housing and a defined ingress-protection target. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Measure missed alerts, range, cue strength, battery life and comfort in the intended home.
ideas.question: What tells the wearer that the band is charged and connected?
ideas.howItWorks: The doorbell sends an event to the receiver. The receiver flashes and vibrates. A status signal shows that the band has power and the link is available.

ideas.title: Parcel arrival notice
ideas.originalProblem: A resident may not notice a parcel has arrived at the door.
ideas.originalSolution: Parcels at the door was one of the group’s recorded topics.
ideas.improvedProblem: A resident may not notice a parcel has arrived at the door.
ideas.reason: A visible movement and separate message make the arrival signal easier to explain and check.

changes.why: Use a load plate with guided travel, a protected switch and a clear received message.

ideas.howItWorks: The parcel lowers a guided spring-return plate onto a switch. Hard travel stops carry excess load. The controller filters contact bounce, sends the notice and re-arms after parcel removal.
ideas.boundary: Add mechanical overload stops, protected wiring and suitable outdoor sealing; keep the walking route clear. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Test light and heavy parcels, off-centre loads, repeated arrivals and acknowledgement.
ideas.question: What stops a heavy parcel crushing the switch?

ideas.title: Crossing reminder cuff
ideas.originalProblem: A person approaching a crossing may need a clear reminder of the steps to follow.
ideas.originalSolution: Crossing the road was another recorded topic, with a small unlabelled cuff-like drawing.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person approaching a crossing may need a clear reminder of the steps to follow.
ideas.reason: The cuff keeps the reminder easy to find. The wearer still needs to check the road.

changes.why: Put a readable reminder on a comfortable adjustable cuff.

ideas.boundary: Use a snag-conscious closure and rounded edges; any visibility claim depends on material and wear testing. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Compare reading speed, comfort and recall with an ordinary reminder card.
ideas.question: Can the wearer read and explain the reminder at a glance?
ideas.howItWorks: The wearer sees the reminder before crossing. The strap holds it in the chosen position and the closure allows easy removal.
ideas.reviewNotice: This proposal is under review. No replacement option has been chosen.

ideas.title: Fire inspection drone
ideas.originalProblem: A response team needs information about a location that is difficult to inspect.
ideas.originalSolution: A drone responds to a fire alert, helps with the fire and searches with a light.
ideas.improvedProblem: A response team needs information about a location that is difficult to inspect.
ideas.reason: Heat and visible context together are more useful than a spotlight alone, while a map link explains where the observation came from.

changes.why: Add paired thermal and visible cameras, location support and an operator-confirmed report.

ideas.howItWorks: Thermal and RGB cameras send paired views. Mapped position, camera direction and range help locate the observation. The operator confirms the map pin, or marks the location uncertain, before deciding what to do.
ideas.boundary: Thermal cannot see through walls or ordinary glass; show uncertainty, use human confirmation and tested aircraft fail-safes. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check image alignment, location error, link loss, battery reserve and representative hot-object false alarms.
proposalParts: Indoor localisation, communications and operator display
ideas.question: How will the operator tell a hot object from a fire and locate it?

ideas.title: Fire detection and alert
ideas.originalProblem: A response team needs an alert that identifies the affected place.
ideas.originalSolution: A scanner detects a fire, alerts drones and proposes guidance for people nearby.
ideas.improvedProblem: A response team needs an alert that identifies the affected place.
ideas.reason: The alert should name the area and let someone confirm they’ve received it.

changes.why: Combine a commissioned detector with a configured room identity and an acknowledged alert.

ideas.boundary: Keep commissioned detection and building alarm functions independent. Operator acknowledgement records receipt; it does not silently disable the alarm. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check room labels, timestamps, missed messages, false alerts and the response to uncertain location.
ideas.question: What information is still useful if the camera view or drone location is uncertain?
ideas.howItWorks: The detector sends an event and its room or zone ID. The system adds time and available camera evidence. The operator acknowledges the report and dispatches or redirects the drone.

ideas.title: Which bin quiz
ideas.originalProblem: People may not know whether an item belongs in recycling or general waste.
ideas.originalSolution: A quiz asks which bin an item goes into.
ideas.improvedProblem: People may not know whether an item belongs in recycling or general waste.
ideas.reason: Explaining the rule helps with new items instead of only memorising a colour.

changes.why: Include the item’s condition and explain the reason after the learner chooses.

ideas.howItWorks: Move the condition pointer and choose a bin aloud. Slide the cover and read the reason matching that condition. Change the item or condition card to compare another case.
ideas.boundary: Keep rules current and include uncertain or special-disposal cases; words and symbols accompany colour. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Ask learners to explain unfamiliar examples and compare the quality of their reasons before and after using the quiz.
ideas.question: What extra question should the quiz ask about an empty but dirty container?

ideas.title: Camera assisted bin feedback
ideas.originalProblem: A wrong item can contaminate the recycling stream.
ideas.originalSolution: The original guard checks items going into one recycling bin and gives red or green feedback.
ideas.improvedProblem: A wrong item can contaminate the recycling stream.
ideas.reason: A second outlet handles confirmed general waste; unknown or special-disposal items stay in the chamber, available for the user to take back.

changes.why: Add a camera inspection chamber and a second general-waste outlet, with a return path for uncertain items.

ideas.boundary: Confidence thresholds need calibration; hold the item in the chamber when uncertain; add jam detection, manual release and accessible stop. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Test known, unknown, dirty, obscured and multiple items; report confusion cases, jams and rejected items.
ideas.question: What should happen when the system cannot recognise an item or tell whether it is clean?
ideas.howItWorks: The camera reads one item in the lit chamber. Software checks a trained class against local rules and asks about missing information. After confirmation, the diverter moves and the gate releases the item.

ideas.title: Reachable light control
ideas.originalProblem: A person in bed may be unable to reach the room light switch.
ideas.originalSolution: A round pendant with side-by-side ON and OFF controls, possible Braille and colour labels.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person in bed may be unable to reach the room light switch.
ideas.reason: Shape, spacing and tactile differences help the person choose the intended control.

changes.why: Use distinguishable controls linked to a compatible light receiver.

ideas.howItWorks: Pressing a cap operates its aligned switch. The transmitter sends the command. The receiver changes the light and can report its state.
ideas.boundary: Avoid a snag-prone neck loop; provide a suitable breakaway or bedside mounting option and secure battery access. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Measure reach, mistaken presses, signal reliability and whether the user knows the light state.
ideas.question: How can the person distinguish ON from OFF without relying on colour?

ideas.title: Firestructor cooking guide
ideas.originalProblem: A person can lose track of a cooking step or leave food unattended.
ideas.originalSolution: A screen gives cooking instructions and recipes.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person can lose track of a cooking step or leave food unattended.
ideas.reason: Clear progress and acknowledgement help the cook see what still needs attention.

changes.why: Show the current step, recipe navigation, a timer and a clear finish sequence.

ideas.boundary: Place the screen outside heat and splash exposure, protect the cable, and define what happens after power or app interruption. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Compare missed steps, time to resume after interruption and clarity of timer acknowledgement with a paper recipe.
ideas.question: How does the display help someone return to the right step after an interruption?
ideas.howItWorks: The cook chooses a recipe and starts a step. Next and Back keep their place. A timer prompts a check, and the finish screen includes checking doneness and switching equipment off.

ideas.title: Phone sleep bed
ideas.originalProblem: A person choosing a phone break wants a clear place to put the phone away.
ideas.originalSolution: A phone-sized bed with blanket, charging pocket, lock and custom headboard.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person choosing a phone break wants a clear place to put the phone away.
ideas.reason: A visible storage path explains where the blanket goes instead of showing a flat panel with nowhere to travel.

changes.why: Use a flexible segmented blanket stored in a foot-end housing and guided along both sides.

ideas.howItWorks: Linked blanket slats slide in the side guides and wrap around a transverse roller in the foot cassette. The pull bar draws them back over the phone. Stops retain the cover and manual opening keeps access available.
ideas.boundary: Keep charging airflow and cable route clear of moving tracks; provide manual opening independent of any timed lock. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check bend radius, full travel, jamming, phone retrieval and cable clearance with actual phone sizes.
proposalParts: Pull bar, stops and manual release

ideas.title: Recycling reward mascot
ideas.originalProblem: People may need clear feedback to learn which items belong in the blue bin.
ideas.originalSolution: Two box-shaped mascots show wrong/correct feedback, use hands as a cue and give stickers or a keychain reward.
ideas.improvedProblem: People may need clear feedback to learn which items belong in the blue bin.
ideas.reason: The feedback can teach the rule while a separate dispenser keeps the reward easy to collect.

changes.why: Link a confirmed sorting choice to the feedback screen and a controlled one-sticker feed.

ideas.boundary: Use rounded fixed decorative hands, a guarded feed path and separate clean reward access. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check feedback clarity, one-at-a-time dispensing, stock detection and learning on new items without rewards.
ideas.question: Will people still make a good choice when no sticker is offered?
ideas.howItWorks: A person confirms the sorting choice and the screen gives feedback. CORRECT enables a matched motor and roller to feed one sticker. WRONG keeps the reward feed off and explains the choice.

ideas.title: Living room caption TV
ideas.originalProblem: A person who cannot hear clearly needs to read what is being said.
ideas.originalSolution: A tabletop caption TV with microphone, bright screen, controller, battery and USB-C charging.
ideas.improvedProblem: A person who cannot hear clearly needs to read what is being said.
ideas.reason: The complete microphone-to-software-to-screen path separates speech recognition from the enclosure design.

changes.why: Fit real speech-to-text hardware/software inside a stable TV-shaped display with accessible controls.

ideas.howItWorks: The microphone captures speech. Speech-to-text software produces words. The display shows large captions; the person can adjust text size, viewing angle and microphone state.
ideas.boundary: Keep microphone and vents unobstructed, provide a clear mute state, and handle transcription uncertainty visibly. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Compare transcription accuracy, delay, readability, glare, microphone placement and real battery runtime.
proposalParts: Supplied processor with compatible speech-to-text software
ideas.question: Is a missed word caused by the microphone, the transcription, or the display?

ideas.title: Articulated fire response car
ideas.originalProblem: A responder needs a way to inspect and reach a dangerous area from a distance.
ideas.originalSolution: A long wheeled vehicle with a two-joint arm carrying an extinguisher.
ideas.improvedProblem: A responder needs a way to inspect and reach a dangerous area from a distance.
ideas.reason: A low cylinder reduces the arm’s payload and tipping tendency while preserving the pupil’s articulated-arm idea.

changes.why: Move the heavy cylinder low on the chassis and put the lighter nozzle on the articulated arm.

ideas.boundary: Use joint stops, hose guards, emergency stop and communication-loss stop. Select a professionally rated suppression system approved for its mounting orientation, fire class and remote actuation. Ask your teacher before building, powering or testing equipment; performance has not been validated.
test: Check full-reach stability, joint loads, hose clearance, braking, link-loss behavior and environmental limits.
ideas.question: How will the car stay stable with the arm fully extended?
ideas.howItWorks: The operator drives and aims using camera views. Geared joints move the nozzle while a flexible hose connects it to the low-mounted cylinder. Discharge requires a separate deliberate command.
proposalParts: Two geared arm joints and nozzle
Protected hose, cameras and operator controls
